perplexity.description:
Released in 1975 on Bearsville Records, Another Live is the second album by Todd Rundgren’s Utopia and the band’s first fully live recording. Musically, the album blends progressive rock with electronic elements, showcasing the group’s technical prowess and eclectic style. The first side features new, original material including standout tracks like “Another Life,” “The Wheel,” and “The Seven Rays,” which highlight the band’s evolving sound and Todd Rundgren’s songwriting. The second side consists of live covers and selections from Rundgren’s solo catalog, demonstrating the group’s versatility and their ability to reinterpret both their own and others’ material in a dynamic live setting.

Another Live marks a transitional moment in Utopia’s discography, being the first album to include future mainstays Roger Powell and Willie Wilcox, while also serving as the last to feature founding members Ralph Schuckett and Mark Klingman. The album’s live format allowed the band to expand their sonic palette, incorporating synthesizers and layered vocals that reflected the growing influence of electronic music in rock. Despite receiving positive critical attention for its musicianship and adventurous arrangements, Another Live did not produce any singles and peaked at #66 on the Billboard 200, reflecting its niche appeal within the progressive and electronic rock scenes of the mid-1970s.
